origins.section: A Data Race Is Two Accesses to One Variable, One a Write, With No Happens-Before Between Them
Code With No Data Race Can Still Race: a Check and an Act Are Two Steps
A Data Race Is Harmless Only When Every Value the Read Can See Gives the Right Answer
A Passing Stress Test Shows Only the Interleavings That Run Produced

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-rates-before-start: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rates-before-start: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rates-before-start: Reference table 'Is it a data race?' row 'written before t.start(), read by t | no', with the definition section naming 'no start or join between the two threads' as the missing edge in the racy example. The page states the row rather than the wording 'every write made before it', but the row covers the stem's case directly.
recorded.prompt:q-atomic-quota: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atomic-quota: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-atomic-quota: 'Code With No Data Race Can Still Race': 'There is no data race left. Volatile reads and writes are synchronization actions...' and 'the check (get() == 0) and the act (set) are two atomic steps, and the other thread can run both of its own between them.' Partly supported only: the option's reason 'since each access is atomic' is not the page's reason. The page says no data race because the accesses are volatile synchronization actions, and explicitly says atomicity alone ('Writes to an int are atomic' is true) does not stop the plain-int race.
recorded.prompt:q-port-read-twice: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-port-read-twice: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-port-read-twice: 'A Data Race Is Harmless Only When...', checksumReadTwice: 'The two reads of checksum are separate racy reads... So the first read may see the checksum and the second 0, and the method returns 0.' Version B matches the page's example exactly.
recorded.prompt:q-green-month: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-green-month: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-green-month: 'A Passing Stress Test Shows Only the Interleavings That Run Produced': 'The two threads leave the latch at slightly different moments, and one call to reference() is short, so the calls seldom overlap', and the test 'fails about one build in a hundred'. This applies the page's measurement of reference() to reserveRoom(), which the stem doesn't describe, but the page's lesson is general (summary: 'A passing stress test shows only the interleavings it produced').

recorded.prompt:q-rates-before-start:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rates-before-start:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rates-before-start:b: Definition section: 'The definition is about order, not about timing: two accesses a second apart with no edge between them still race.' The claim (no race) is true; the reason (no overlap in time) is the one the page rejects.
recorded.prompt:q-rates-before-start:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rates-before-start:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rates-before-start:c: The JLS 17.4.5 definition and the table row 'written before t.start(), read by t | no' carry no condition about the class being thread-safe; the map's internal fields are plain variables ordered by the start edge. Refuted by the general definition, not by an explicit sentence; the 'says' phrase 'whatever the class' is an inference the page does not state in those words.
recorded.prompt:q-rates-before-start:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-rates-before-start:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-rates-before-start:d: Same 'order, not timing' sentence, plus the table showing start() as an edge with no lock involved ('written before t.start(), read by t | no' sits separately from the lock rows).
recorded.prompt:q-atomic-quota:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atomic-quota:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-atomic-quota:a: Table row 'a volatile field, or an Atomic* class through its volatile-mode methods (get, set, compareAndSet, ...) | no', and 'Volatile reads and writes are synchronization actions, which are not counted as data races'. No lock is required.
recorded.prompt:q-atomic-quota:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atomic-quota:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-atomic-quota:b: 'the JMM puts them in one total order, and each read returns the latest write in it (JLS 17.4.4, 17.4.7). No read of ref is stale.' The page does not talk about CPU caches, but it refutes stale reads of atomic values.
recorded.prompt:q-atomic-quota:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-atomic-quota:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-atomic-quota:d: Definition section: 'incrementAndGet() is one atomic read-modify-write on a volatile field, so two calls never return the same number.' The claim (no data race) is true; the reason (lost increment) is refuted.
recorded.prompt:q-port-read-twice:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-port-read-twice:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-port-read-twice:a: 'No write is undone; the second read simply sees an older one.' The claim (can return 0) is true; the reason (write lost) is the one the page rejects.
recorded.prompt:q-port-read-twice:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-port-read-twice:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-port-read-twice:c: 'So the first read may see the checksum and the second 0'. The second read can see an older value than the first, and the page says this is allowed by the JLS.
recorded.prompt:q-port-read-twice:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-port-read-twice:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-port-read-twice:d: 'Each may see the initial 0, which is the last write ordered before it, or the other thread's write, which isn't ordered against it.' Another thread's write being made does not oblige this thread's later read to see it; see also 'a read may also see an older write than the latest one'.
recorded.prompt:q-green-month:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-green-month:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-green-month:a: 'It needs no data race' (check-then-act section), and the naive test run against the AtomicInteger version (no data race) failed 3 to 14 of 1000.
recorded.prompt:q-green-month:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-green-month:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-green-month:c: The section heading and summary say a passing stress test shows only the interleavings it produced, and the calls 'seldom overlap'. With 1000 runs failing only 3 to 14 times, 40 runs cannot be expected to cover every order.
recorded.prompt:q-green-month:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-green-month:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-green-month:d: 'A test that makes one attempt fails about one build in a hundred.' At that rate the bug probably does not show in 40 runs. The page does not compute this; the reader must (0.99^40 is about 0.67). The 'says' line 'usually all pass' is that inference, not page text.
